::: {#exm-false-positive-prob}
#### False positives accumulate with the number of tests

With $\siglevel = 0.05$,
@thm-false-positive-prob gives the chance of at least one false positive
among $m$ independent tests of true null hypotheses:

```{r}
#| label: false-positive-prob
#| code-fold: false
alpha <- 0.05
m_values <- c(1, 5, 14, 20, 100, 2308)
data.frame(
  m = m_values,
  prob_at_least_one = 1 - (1 - alpha)^m_values
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 4,
    col.names = c("Tests m", "Pr(at least one false positive)")
  )
```

The chance first passes one half at `r ceiling(log(0.5) / log(1 - alpha))` tests.
With 2308 tests, the number of genes in the Khan data,
the chance of no false positive at all is `r format((1 - alpha)^2308, digits = 2)`,
so a false positive is a near certainty.
:::
